Alright, I’ve just added the new “effort-menu” kind to the `CommandResult` type in `commands.ts`. That was a necessary first step because the UI now needs to be able to return this new kind when the user selects an effort level from the menu. However, just adding the type isn’t enough – the actual command definitions need to reflect the new commands that the rest of the codebase expects.

Looking back at the recent changes I made elsewhere:
- In `agent.ts` I added support for `onTodos` callbacks and richer usage reporting.
- In `prompts.ts` I tweaked the system prompt wording.
- I introduced a full markdown renderer in `components/Markdown.tsx`.
- I also mentioned that the commands module now supports “/thought-show” and “/thought-hide” as well as an expanded effort menu (including the new “ultracode” level).

Given those updates, the `COMMANDS` array in `src/commands.ts` is still missing entries for the new thought toggles and the expanded effort options. If I don’t add them, any UI that renders the command list or any logic that validates user input will reject these commands, leading to “unknown command” errors. Moreover, the effort command’s description should now list “ultracode” as a valid option.

Another subtle point: users often type abbreviated commands (e.g., “/he” for “help” or “/th” for “thought-show”). The existing code only does an exact match on the command name, so abbreviations aren’t resolved. To make the CLI more user‑friendly, I should add a small helper that first checks for an exact match and, if none is found, looks for a unique prefix. If the prefix matches exactly one command, we can safely resolve it; otherwise we return null to signal ambiguity or unknown command.

Therefore, the next logical edit is twofold:
1. Update the `COMMANDS` array to include the new entries:
   - Extend the `effort` command description to mention “ultracode”.
   - Add `thought-show` and `thought-hide` with appropriate descriptions.
2. Append a `resolveCommand` utility function that implements the exact‑match‑then‑unique‑prefix logic.

I’ll use the `Edit` tool with `replace_all: false` to replace the block that defines `COMMANDS`. I’ll keep the existing ordering for readability, just inserting the new entries where they belong. After the array, I’ll add the new function definition. This should integrate cleanly with the rest of the codebase and enable the new UI features I introduced earlier.

export const COMMANDS: CommandDef[] = [
  { name: "help", description: "show commands and keybindings" },
  { name: "clear", description: "clear conversation and screen" },
  { name: "compact", description: "summarize history to free context" },
  { name: "effort", description: "set effort: low | medium | high | max | ultracode" },
  { name: "model", description: "show model configuration" },
  { name: "yolo", description: "toggle auto-approve for all actions" },
  { name: "thought-show", description: "show the model's thinking while it works" },
  { name: "thought-hide", description: "hide thinking, show the compact spinner" },
  { name: "diagnostics", description: "diagnostics status + verify trace chain" },
  { name: "no-diagnostics", description: "opt out of diagnostic traces" },
  { name: "memory", description: "show persistent memory" },
  { name: "skills", description: "list saved skills" },
  { name: "sessions", description: "list recent sessions" },
  { name: "resume", description: "resume a session: /resume <id>" },
  { name: "usage", description: "token usage this session" },
  { name: "init", description: "generate an AGENTS.md for this project" },
  { name: "intro", description: "replay the startup animation" },
  { name: "quit", description: "exit glint" },
];

/** Resolve a possibly-abbreviated command name: exact match wins, then a
 * unique prefix; returns null when unknown or ambiguous. */
export function resolveCommand(name: string): string | null {
  if (COMMANDS.some((c) => c.name === name)) return name;
  const matches = COMMANDS.filter((c) => c.name.startsWith(name));
  return matches.length === 1 ? matches[0].name : null;
}
